item.text:
**Bottom Line**
The 2024 record is mostly negative on 3B.5. Sharif did use some force and security measures through formal channels against real threats, but the stronger evidence shows emergency-style controls and policing being used for intimidation, mass arrests, internet shutdowns, discriminatory enforcement, and weakened judicial checks. I found no strong evidence that he built a narrowly lawful framework for surveillance or emergency powers.

**Accepted Items**
- [PM for collective efforts to eliminate menace of terrorism](https://www.radio.gov.pk/22-06-2024/pm-for-collective-efforts-to-eliminate-menace-of-terrorism) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-06-22  
  Claim-level summary: Sharif launched a national counterterrorism campaign with provincial consensus and said the armed forces would be supported with necessary resources. This is the best pro-lawful-use item, because it shows security mobilization through collective authority rather than obviously ad hoc coercion.  
  Question IDs: `3B.5`, also `3B.2`

- [Civil-military leadership reiterate commitment to work together for prosperous, secure Pakistan](https://www.radio.gov.pk/15-03-2024/civil-military-leadership-reiterate-commitment-to-work-together-for-prosperous-secure-pakistan) | Radio Pakistan | 2024-03-15  
  Claim-level summary: Sharif said the government would provide all resources required for operational readiness after briefings on the security environment and counterterrorism operations. This supports a narrow-security rationale, though it does not itself show safeguards against abuse.  
  Question IDs: `3B.5`, also `3B.2`

- [Election-day internet shutdown is a reckless attack on peoples' rights](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/pakistan-election-day-internet-shutdown-is-a-reckless-attack-on-peoples-rights/) | Amnesty International | 2024-02-08  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty condemned the telecom and mobile internet shutdown as a rights violation during the election period. This is direct evidence of coercive administrative control used against a politically charged public.  
  Question IDs: `3B.5`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`

- [Pakistan government intensifies crackdown on political dissent](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/09/pakistan-government-intensifies-crackdown-political-dissent) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-09  
  Claim-level summary: HRW reported over 500 arrests, tear gas, roadblocks, mobile internet cuts, and arrests for peaceful protest. That is strong evidence that security tools were used for intimidation and collective repression, not narrowly targeted law enforcement.  
  Question IDs: `3B.5`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`

- [Pakistani police detain two parliamentarians in swoop on ex-PM Khan's party](https://theprint.in/world/pakistani-police-detain-two-parliamentarians-in-swoop-on-ex-pm-khans-party/2260202/) | Reuters / ThePrint | 2024-09-10  
  Claim-level summary: Police detained PTI parliamentarians after a rally demanding Khan’s release. This is evidence of administrative and policing powers being used against opponents, with no clear contemporaneous signal of restraint or independent review.  
  Question IDs: `3B.5`, also `3B.2`

- [Pakistan authorities must end escalating attacks on minority Ahmadiyya community](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/end-escalating-attacks-on-minority-ahmadiyya-community/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-21  
  Claim-level summary: Amnesty documented arbitrary arrests, police harassment, and orders blocking Ahmadi rites. This is the clearest evidence that local administrative power and policing were being used to control and punish a minority community.  
  Question IDs: `3B.5`, also `3B.1`, `3B.2`

- [Pakistan's government curbs judiciary's power after alleged harassment of MPs](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/oct/21/pakistans-government-curbs-judiciarys-power-after-alleged-harassment-of-mps) | The Guardian | 2024-10-21  
  Claim-level summary: The 26th amendment was passed amid allegations of intimidation and abductions of MPs, and critics said it reduced judicial independence. That cuts against narrow, lawful use of emergency or security powers because it weakens oversight of abuse by politically protected actors.  
  Question IDs: `3B.5`, also `3B.4`, `3B.2`

- [2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Pakistan](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128431.html) | U.S. Department of State | 2024  
  Claim-level summary: The report says the government rarely took credible steps to identify and punish officials who committed abuses. This is broad evidence that formal security and administrative systems were not being tightly constrained by accountability.  
  Question IDs: `3B.5`, also `3B.4`, `3B.1`, `3B.2`

- [World Report 2024: Pakistan](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/pakistan) | Human Rights Watch | 2024  
  Claim-level summary: HRW reported that Sharif ordered measures to improve sanitation and healthcare in Lahore Central Prison and vowed prison reforms nationwide. This is the main positive counterpoint, but it looks reactive and limited rather than like a built, lawful control framework.  
  Question IDs: `3B.5`, also `3B.4`

**Search Gap**
I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Sharif built a narrowly lawful system for emergency powers, surveillance, or anti-terror administration with credible judicial or civilian checks. The available record is instead dominated by coercive shutdowns, political policing, and weakened judicial independence.
